Sleep is the tide that reclaims us nightly, pulling consciousness out to some vast and unmappable sea. We resist it as children, surrender to it as the weary, and wake from it as strangers to ourselves, blinking at the ceiling as though it were a country we had never visited before.

The dream is a forger, assembling counterfeit realities from the debris of the day. Your mother appears in a house that is not her house. The corridor extends beyond architecture. You are late for an examination in a subject you have never studied... and the anxiety is authentic, smuggled from the sleeping mind into the waking body like contraband.

Insomnia is the cruelest cartography. The clock maps the hours in luminous numerals while the mind traverses its most desolate territories. Three in the morning is a country with no embassy, no consulate, no fellow travelers.

But dawn arrives. It always arrives. The light seeps beneath the curtain like a pardon slipped under a cell door, and the sleeper surfaces, carrying fragments of the deep... unremembered, essential, dissolving already on the tongue of wakefulness.
